before:
The only fully working airport on Lombok, and the way in for the Gili Islands, Mandalika and Mount Rinjani. It is at Tanak Awu in Central Lombok, about 6 km from Praya and 27 km from Mataram, so transfer times depend a good deal on which end of the island a client is staying.

It opened in 2011, replacing Selaparang Airport at Ampenan on the west coast. The runway is 2,750 metres and takes wide bodies up to an A330 or a 767.

The terminal was rebuilt for the 2022 MotoGP at Mandalika and is now a different proposition: 43,501 square metres against 24,123 before, with capacity lifted from 3.25 million passengers a year to 7 million. There are 46 check in counters and seven boarding gates, five of them with jet bridges.

Flights run to Jakarta, Denpasar and Surabaya, with international services to Malaysia and Singapore. It is also known as Zainuddin Abdul Madjid International Airport, so both names turn up in supplier systems.
after:
Lombok's only fully working airport, serving the Gili Islands, Mandalika and Mount Rinjani. It is at Tanak Awu in Central Lombok, near Praya and about 27 km from Mataram, so transfer times depend a good deal on which end of the island a client is staying.

Opened in 2011, it replaced Selaparang Airport in Mataram. The runway is now 3,300 metres, long enough for wide bodies up to a Boeing 777.

Its terminal was enlarged for the MotoGP races at Mandalika, from 24,123 to 43,501 square metres, with room for about 7 million passengers a year.

Flights run to Jakarta, Denpasar and Surabaya, with international services to Malaysia and Singapore. It is also known as Zainuddin Abdul Madjid International Airport, so both names turn up in supplier systems.
